dist/manifest.json lists artifacts, reports and status next to the plan, envelope and logs. Test and quality failures stop artifact collection. Package receipts detect archive changes between packing and collection. Missing or invalid required reports fail the build, even with task overrides. inspect checks bundle integrity, not trust or release eligibility. Earlier bundles are kept under .oyzu/history.

For a conventional npm workspace with a publishable root and package-local builds, select the node/package builder. It runs on your machine, without Docker. builds: package: {uses: node/package} oyzu --json build package --full --no-cache oyzu inspect dist Keep the genuine package-lock.json. The builder produces one archive and one JUnit/LCOV report pair for each publishable package. A project with a root, an app member and a shared member produces three archives and six reports. Supported: Windows x64, with Node 22.23.3 and npm 11.11.0. Each package declares its native version, exports and files. Builds are flat literal copies (for example copy source.cjs dist.cjs on Windows), and each package has implicit Node tests. Lint and read-only format checks need working project scripts or provisioned checkers. The builder does not install fallback quality tools. How it works: Oyzu runs npm ci --ignore-scripts in a private workspace to read membership and installed links, then fixes each package's version, commands, archive location and report location. The ordinary npm ci then runs once with native lifecycle scripts and Oyzu hooks. Its result is checked before versions and local references are rewritten in the private copy. Packages build in dependency order (shared, then app, then root). Native pre, build and post scripts and selected Oyzu hooks run as usual. Each package's implicit Node tests write its own JUnit and LCOV. A publishable root cannot borrow a member's report. npm pack --json --ignore-scripts runs after the required checks, writing to a fresh output location. Your source and native locks are unchanged. The first normal build may add the plugin selection to oyzu.lock. Use each artifact's recorded path, digest and version instead of guessing npm's file names. Installing the three archives into an empty project with an empty npm cache and --offline works, and root imports through app and shared. Producer-side downloads still follow your configuration and network controls. Problem What to do Stale or missing lock, or an invalid installed workspace link Repair the manifests and lock with npm and retry. Replaced install task, or install unavailable or disabled Use the ordinary npm ci task. The builder refuses other install setups before preparing the workspace. Failed build or check, missing package report, or an invalid pack file list Fix that package. A failed required step blocks all archive export. Aggregate or opaque build, replaced build or test task, or a write outside the package Not supported by this builder. Package-local ownership rules stay in force. Not supported yet: private aggregation roots, authored aggregate tasks, framework builds, pnpm and Yarn in this mode (see their pages), macOS, Windows ARM64, Linux hosts and Linux ARM64. For isolated builds see captured workspace packages.

Note: Experimental. Supported on Linux x86_64 (GNU) only. Windows, macOS and ARM64 are not supported for this profile. A publishable root and one shared member each build with tsc -p tsconfig.json. The root imports shared through its package metadata, so shared compiles first. Each package's main or exports and types point to JavaScript and declarations under its own dist/. Tested with Node 22.23.3, npm 11.11.0 and TypeScript 7.0.2. Keep contained rootDir and outDir values with separate source and output folders, and set noEmitOnError: true: { "compilerOptions": { "target": "ES2022", "module": "NodeNext", "moduleResolution": "NodeNext", "rootDir": "src", "outDir": "dist", "declaration": true, "noEmitOnError": true }, "include": ["src/**/*.ts"] } Set type: commonjs in each package (the CommonJS output is what is supported). Select node/package and run the build as above. You get two npm archives and four JUnit/LCOV reports. A TypeScript error in shared stops the root compile and both archives. TypeScript owns type resolution, diagnostics, emitted files and exit codes. Before building, Oyzu checks every JavaScript and declaration output path, and any build-info path, against protected and prepared-owner paths inside the package's dist/. Incremental and composite builds need an explicit, checked tsBuildInfoFile. noEmitOnError alone does not guarantee the compiler writes nothing. Configuration inheritance (extends), project references, outFile, JSON-module copying, unchecked emission and extra command-line forms are refused.

For isolated builds, select the node/package builder and an installed Node plugin package whose engine includes the coordinator and execution runtimes: builds: workspace: uses: node/package Keep tool requests in oyzu.toml or native pins, and the genuine npm lock next to the workspace manifests. Build YAML contains no tool pins. For example, the tested project requests Node 22.23.3 and npm 11.11.0 under [tools]. With the npm image and tool archives available: oyzu --json build workspace --isolated --platform linux/amd64 --full --no-cache --image npm=<image> An unadopted package makes oyzu pin refuse with PLUGIN_NOT_ADOPTED. Run a normal build once to adopt the plugin and create oyzu.lock, then keep that lock for later --frozen runs. Captured publishable-root workspaces use a Linux amd64 worker: Coordinator Node / npm Supported profile Windows x64 22.23.3 / 11.11.0 Publishable root and two members, default owner reports Linux x64 22.23.4 / 10.9.9 Publishable root and one member, aggregate tests with explicit owner report redirection Each publishable owner produces an archive and requires its own JUnit/LCOV pair. The archives can be installed offline outside the source checkout. Other coordinator platforms are unsupported here. Native-host packages use the separate native profile. How it works: Oyzu reads npm's prepared membership and installed links, then fixes each package's version, Node test files, report locations and archive slot. Versions and local references are rewritten only in the private copy. Dependency builds are ordered, and npm packs each package. npm still runs each package's prebuild, build and postbuild. Oyzu's build hooks wrap the whole build once. Each publishable package needs discoverable implicit Node tests. Reports are collected before packing and export. Your manifests and the lock are unchanged. Package-local copy builds and hooks are recognized. Replaced build or test tasks, and a root aggregate test, are refused before any task or hook runs. Dependency preparation may already have happened. Dependency or package-test failures block archive delivery.

An opaque root build, or one that is not package-local, runs its original npm run build once at the workspace root. It does not add member builds. Recognized package-local builds keep their ordering. A local root with opaque or nonlocal member dispatch is refused. The root script must produce every package's outputs. Each package still needs implicit Node tests and its own JUnit and LCOV before packing. Protected configuration writes, writes to another package's output, and reads or writes outside the source are refused even inside a coarse root body. An explicit npm --workspace call may write only its own member's ordinary outputs through its lifecycle and same-owner helpers. That permission does not carry to later root commands. Changing directory or --prefix does not change which package owns the writes. You can also replace the whole build with a task in oyzu.toml: [tasks."workspace:build"] argv = ["npm", "run", "build"] Even identical argv counts as a replacement, so all native member builds are skipped. npm lifecycle scripts run only if your command invokes npm. Oyzu build hooks wrap the selected build once. No setting picks the build route.

An explicit root test script runs unchanged, once, with pretest and posttest. No implicit package suites run afterward. A workspace:test task replacement can run the same script. Either way, the script must write JUnit and LCOV for every package. Default report locations use the package name. For g17-shared, the member writes .oyzu/plugin-reports/package-g17-shared/junit.xml and coverage.lcov under its own folder, such as packages/shared/.oyzu/plugin-reports/package-g17-shared/. The root and other members have their own named pairs. No single OYZU_TEST_REPORT or OYZU_COVERAGE_REPORT is provided for these multiple packages. To collect an owner's reports from custom locations, name its frozen report key in each declaration's owner. Paths are relative to the selected task's working directory; a path never selects an owner. For example, an aggregate command for g17-app can write its pair under reports/app/: min_oyzu_version = "0.4.0" [tasks."workspace:test"] argv = ["npm", "run", "test"] reports = [ { owner = "package-g17-app", kind = "test", format = "junit", path = "reports/app/junit.xml" }, { owner = "package-g17-app", kind = "coverage", format = "lcov", path = "reports/app/coverage.lcov" }, ] Use the exact owner key from the planned report identity, such as workspace:test:package-g17-app. Other owners keep their default pairs, and an omitted kind keeps that owner's default file. The command must write the selected files itself; redirection changes collection paths without rewriting its body. Every redirect needs a resolvable owner, its native report format and one contained literal path. Unknown or missing owners, repeated owner/kind mappings, and paths shared by multiple reports are refused before any action or hook runs. Path comparisons ignore ASCII case, including on Windows; defaults participate in collision checks. Fix the named mapping or remove it to use the default. Dependency capture may already have happened. A missing or invalid required file still fails the build even if the aggregate command exits successfully; another owner's report or a file at the old default path cannot replace it. Without a root aggregate test, npm workspaces keep implicit suites.

Archive versions come from Oyzu's version rules, not from the manifests. For example, with every manifest at 0.1.0, the root might get 0.0.0-dev.<source-id> and the members 0.1.0-dev.<source-id>. Dependency references inside the archives match.

Every workspace member is packaged as its own archive, under its package name and a version derived from its version. A root without "private": true is packaged too. A private root is not. Members that can't be packaged this way fail with an error naming every affected member and path. Two conditions fail: A package name is used by more than one member, or by a publishable root and a member. A member's version is latest. Oyzu resolves npm membership first, before acquiring dependencies, and reports both conditions in one error with the code NPM_WORKSPACE_MEMBER_NAMES. Paths are relative to the workspace root. For the npm-member-names example: NPM_WORKSPACE_MEMBER_NAMES: npm workspace members need distinct package names and real versions to be packaged package name "@oyzu-example/core" is used by "." (publishable workspace root), "packages/core" version "latest" is not a package version: "test", "test/installation" Remedy: rename packages so each name is used once, or mark the workspace root "private": true so the root is not packaged; give each listed member a semver "version" such as "0.0.0" in its package.json; "private": true on a member does not exclude it, because every member is packaged. In oyzu build, this text appears inside the npm dependency preparation failed diagnostic. Nothing is acquired, no artifact is produced and the source is unchanged. oyzu run workspace tasks stop with the same error. oyzu run list does not resolve membership and is unaffected. To fix it: Rename members so each package name is used once. If the root only coordinates the workspace, "private": true on the root also works, because a private root is not packaged. Give each latest member a semver version, such as 0.0.0. Marking the member "private": true does not help. Private members are packaged like any other, and excluding a member from packaging is not supported. Other messages: npm itself refuses members that share a name. Oyzu takes them from npm's report and lists them with the other problems. If npm can't list the remaining members after the duplicates are excluded (this happens when a duplicate's path contains glob syntax), the error says that other members were not checked. Other invalid member names or versions fail with npm workspace requires a valid native name/version. A publishable root with an invalid name or version fails with Publishable npm workspace root requires a valid native name/version. This check covers npm workspaces only. pnpm and Yarn keep their own checks.

Frameworks other than Node's runner, Jest, Vitest and Mocha, full framework configuration inheritance, cyclic workspace graphs, affected selection, caching and publication are not supported. Direct test bundles contain host test results, not the versioned artifacts of an isolated build. Platform support is listed with each mode above. Platforms not listed there are not supported yet.

Yarn Classic workspace builds pnpm workspace builds Workspace test bundles for pnpm and Yarn Classic direct tests Node applications for a private root that builds one application directory Mocha, Node quality and direct tests

CLI reference Published from the canonical docs/reference/nuget-sessions.md file. Features marked experimental remain experimental; check support limitations before relying on them. Use this when dotnet restore and dotnet build should use a private NuGet feed without a password in nuget.config or environment variables. Each time you run dotnet through oyzu, oyzu asks a local credential agent which feed to use and supplies the password to NuGet through a credential plugin. Note: Experimental. You need a credential agent running on the same machine; oyzu doesn't include one. Supported on Linux with the .NET 8 SDK and Bash. .NET builds with oyzu build don't use this yet.

Add the agent's address to your user or administrator configuration (not the project's oyzu.toml): [nuget] sessionEndpoint = "http://127.0.0.1:43199/session" Setting Values Default Meaning nuget.sessionEndpoint http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<path>, no user name, password, query or fragment Not set The local agent to ask for sessions. Remove it to go back to plain dotnet Project, local and command-line configuration and profiles can't set this value. User configuration isn't read in CI, so this doesn't work there.

With a .NET 8 SDK installed: oyzu exec -- /usr/share/dotnet/dotnet restore --locked-mode oyzu exec -- /usr/share/dotnet/dotnet build --no-restore # or, with dotnet on PATH: eval "$(oyzu activate bash)" dotnet build Only restore and build are supported. --help, --version, --info, --list-sdks and --list-runtimes run without asking the agent. Anything else, including dotnet nuget push and dotnet publish, fails with NUGET_OPERATION_UNSUPPORTED. Publish packages with oyzu publish.

Sends the agent a POST with {"directory": "<working dir>", "tool": "dotnet", "arguments": [...]}. This happens on every run, including build --no-restore. Reads the agent's answer: { "feed": "https://packages.example.com/nuget/v3/index.json", "credentialScope": "https://packages.example.com/nuget/", "username": "reader", "credentialEndpoint": "http://127.0.0.1:43199/credential/session" } Field Rules feed HTTP(S), no credentials, query, fragment or ;. Must be under credentialScope credentialScope Same origin as feed, ending in / credentialEndpoint On 127.0.0.1. A GET returns the password as UTF-8 text Compiles a small bundled C# credential plugin with your SDK (no extra packages or runtimes needed) and writes a temporary nuget.config with only that feed. Runs dotnet with that feed and plugin. Restore sources from MSBuild properties and project files are replaced, so the agent's feed wins, but project files aren't edited. When NuGet asks for credentials, the plugin fetches the password, but only for URLs inside credentialScope. Removes the temporary files when dotnet finishes or fails. MSBuild node reuse is turned off for the run. NuGet's package and HTTP caches work as usual.

The password never goes into the generated config, command arguments or environment variables. It travels through NuGet's plugin channel and is in the build's memory, so build code can read it. Treat the temporary session files as sensitive even though they don't contain the password. Read-only access has to be enforced by the feed account the agent uses. Plugin failures show a generic message, not the agent's response. Denial or an unreachable agent stops the command before dotnet starts, with no fallback.
dotnet's output and exit code pass through unchanged. With --json, they're captured in the usual oyzu exec result.

Code Cause Fix NATIVE_SESSION_CONFIG The endpoint is set in project or local configuration Move it to user or administrator configuration NATIVE_SESSION_UNAVAILABLE The agent can't be reached Start the agent and retry NATIVE_SESSION_DENIED The agent refused the request Get access granted; don't work around the agent NATIVE_SESSION_INVALID The endpoint or credential endpoint isn't 127.0.0.1 HTTP, or the response is too large Fix the endpoint or the agent NUGET_SESSION_INVALID The feed or scope in the response isn't valid Fix the agent's response NUGET_SESSION_PREPARE The plugin couldn't be compiled Install a working .NET 8 SDK with its reference packs NUGET_ROUTING_CONFLICT You passed --source/-s, --configfile, RestoreSources or RestoreConfigFile Remove the override NUGET_OPERATION_UNSUPPORTED The command isn't restore or build Use a supported command

One feed and one credential scope per run. Multiple feeds, source mappings, custom settings files and other credential plugins aren't supported. Custom MSBuild targets that make their own network calls aren't covered. Temporary files may be left behind if oyzu is killed. Linux, .NET 8 and Bash only. Windows, macOS and other SDK versions aren't supported yet.
.NET builds Private Python indexes

CLI reference Published from the canonical docs/reference/oci-indices.md file. Features marked experimental remain experimental; check support limitations before relying on them. When a docker/image build lists several platforms, Oyzu builds one image per platform and also writes a single OCI index that points at all of them. No extra setting is needed. The index describes the complete set of platform images in one archive. Note: Image builds are experimental. Current support is linux/x86_64 only. ARM64 targets are unsupported, so the multi-platform example below is illustrative and cannot be used as a supported build today. Platform scope: Use an x64 host and supported x64 build targets. ARM64 is unsupported. Feature-specific limits are listed in the support matrix.

# build.yaml builds: image: uses: docker/image platforms: [linux/x86_64, linux/arm64] oyzu build image --plan oyzu build image oyzu inspect dist The Dockerfile in this example contains FROM scratch and COPY. A Dockerfile with RUN still needs a worker that matches the platform it builds. See Docker image inputs for how to set up the Docker toolchain and BuildKit worker. oyzu run list still shows only the builder's tasks. The index is made by an extra assemble-index step in the build plan, which appears after the per-platform image steps. oyzu build --plan shows the declared platform variants. The index step itself appears once the build is prepared.

An index needs at least two platform variants of one target, all selected for the build, with image outputs that share one output name and version. Each other variant axis forms its own group. Two runtime versions, for example, each get their own complete index. A target with one platform just keeps its image. If you select only some platforms of a larger family, Oyzu does not build a partial index. See matrix selection.

Each index produces: An artifact of kind: "oci-index" with media type application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json. A file at dist/<index-id>/any/<family>-<version>.oci.tar. It sits under any because it spans several platforms (see the bundle layout). A file digest and size, plus ociDigest, the digest of the root index. Read target IDs and paths from the plan or manifest instead of building the names yourself. The index target uses builder oyzu/oci-index and has platform: null. Null means a collection of platforms, not an artifact without a platform. Tools that read the plan or manifest must handle such targets. Ordinary image targets always have a concrete platform.

Every per-platform image must build successfully first. Oyzu then checks each image archive's hash, size, OCI contents, digest and platform. It writes one archive that holds the unchanged image manifests, configs and layers (shared blobs stored once) and a sorted index. The same inputs always produce the same archive. Assembly runs inside the CLI, reads the archives without extracting them and uses no network. It allows up to 256 input images and a 10 GiB archive. It does not run in a container, so it has no separate CPU, memory or time limits. In the plan, this step is identified by extensions["oyzu.dev/oci-index"] and does not carry an executor mode. Execution handles it as in-process assembly; the platform image actions retain their own executor modes and worker checks. If one platform fails, the index is not built, but the other platforms' images remain available to inspect. An index never leaves out a failed platform. Fix the failure and build again. oyzu inspect dist checks that the index lists exactly the required images from successful builds. It rejects a complete-looking index that is missing a platform, and a bundle that is missing a planned index. Inspecting only the .oci.tar file checks its own contents but cannot tell whether the platform set was the required one. Neither check says who built it.

The supported platform is linux/x86_64. Retained ARM64 examples describe the generic index contract only. Images with RUN for a foreign platform are not supported. Oyzu does not push an index to a registry. Publishing pushes single-platform images only. ABI and CPU feature negotiation are not supported. The archive follows the OCI image index specification.
Docker image inputs and offline builds Build bundles Matrix builds

CLI reference Published from the canonical docs/reference/oci-sessions.md file. Features marked experimental remain experimental; check support limitations before relying on them. Use this when Helm or BuildKit (buildctl) should pull charts and images from private OCI registries without credentials in Docker or Helm config files. Each time you run helm or buildctl through oyzu, oyzu asks a local credential agent which registries are allowed, and a credential helper hands the client credentials only when it needs them. The agent can also redirect images and charts to approved mirrors and grant access to BuildKit cache references. Note: Experimental. You need a credential agent running on the same machine; oyzu doesn't include one, and it doesn't install Helm or BuildKit. Supported on Linux (BuildKit 0.25.0).

Add the agent's address to your user or administrator configuration (not the project's oyzu.toml): [oci] sessionEndpoint = "http://127.0.0.1:43199/session" Setting Values Default Meaning oci.sessionEndpoint http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<path>, no user name, password, query or fragment Not set The local agent to ask for sessions. Remove it to go back to plain Helm and BuildKit Project, local and command-line configuration and profiles can't set this value. User configuration isn't read in CI, so this doesn't work there. OYZU_USER_CONFIG can point at a different user configuration file.

oyzu exec -- /usr/local/bin/helm pull oci://registry.example.com/charts/sample --version 0.1.0 oyzu exec -- /usr/local/bin/buildctl --addr tcp://builder.example.com:1234 build \ --frontend dockerfile.v0 --local context=. --local dockerfile=. \ --output type=local,dest=dist In an activated Bash shell, oyzu adds shims for helm and buildctl found on PATH, so bare helm and buildctl go through oyzu too. Each run asks the agent for a fresh session. Client Supported Helm pull, dependency, template BuildKit Commands with build --help, -h and helm version run without asking the agent. Other executables run normally. Configure TLS for your registries and builder yourself. These are refused: --registry-config, --username and --password (OCI_ROUTING_CONFLICT); push=true and registry image outputs (OCI_OPERATION_UNSUPPORTED). Publish with oyzu publish.

Sends the agent a POST with {"directory": "<working dir>", "tool": "helm" or "buildctl", "arguments": [...]}. This happens on every run, even when content is cached. Reads the agent's answer: { "credentialEndpoint": "http://127.0.0.1:43199/credential/session", "registries": ["registry.example.com"] } Writes a temporary Helm and Docker config whose credHelpers point each listed registry at oyzu's credential helper, and puts the helper on the child's PATH. When the client needs credentials, the helper POSTs {"registry": "<host>"} to credentialEndpoint, which must answer {"username": "...", "secret": "..."}. Removes the temporary files when the command finishes or fails. The agent decides what's allowed, including for cached content. oyzu doesn't evaluate policy or read every manifest itself.

The agent's answer can also include a projection that redirects sources and grants cache access. Replace the digest placeholders with real digests: { "credentialEndpoint": "http://127.0.0.1:43199/credential/session", "registries": ["mirror.example.com", "cache.example.com"], "projection": { "imageMappings": [{ "from": "origin.example.com/team/base@sha256:<64-hex-digits>", "to": "mirror.example.com/team/base@sha256:<same-64-hex-digits>" }], "cacheReads": ["cache.example.com/team/build:shared"], "cacheWrites": [] } }
documents.s: Admitted source projection and cache operations

documents.t: With imageMappings, oyzu writes a temporary BuildKit source policy and passes it with --source-policy-file: Each exact, fully qualified image reference is replaced with its mapped destination. Destinations must be pinned by digest and on a listed registry. A pinned source can't change digest. Every other image source is denied. Your Dockerfile and the BuildKit daemon configuration aren't changed. Passing your own --source-policy-file conflicts with this. If a mapped image is missing from the mirror, the build fails; it doesn't fall back to the original reference. HTTP and Git sources and network access from RUN steps aren't covered. Without a projection, or with no image mappings, oyzu only supplies credentials and doesn't restrict images.

oyzu exec -- buildctl --addr tcp://builder:1234 build \ --frontend dockerfile.v0 --local context=. --local dockerfile=. \ --output type=local,dest=dist \ --import-cache type=registry,ref=cache.example.com/team/build:shared --import-cache type=registry,ref=... needs that exact reference in cacheReads. --export-cache type=registry,ref=... needs that exact reference in cacheWrites. Both --flag value and --flag=value forms work. Missing grants fail before BuildKit runs. local and inline caches work as usual. Other cache types, or unclear ones, fail. Cache grants don't allow publishing images. The helper supplies one identity per registry host for a run, so the agent should issue one identity that covers everything allowed on that host. Use separate hosts or runs if you need different credentials. A cache hit means BuildKit reused a result; it doesn't mean tests ran again.

For Helm, the agent returns helmMappings instead: { "helmMappings": [{ "from": "origin.example.com/charts/service", "to": "mirror.example.com/charts/service" }] } This works for one helm pull oci://... reference. oyzu replaces just that argument and keeps the version and other options. The destination host must be listed. Chart.yaml and lock files aren't changed. Pull the chart first, then render the local archive with Helm. Mapped dependency and template commands fail as unsupported.

Credentials never go into the temporary config files. They pass through the helper into the client's memory, so the client can read them. Read-only access has to be enforced by the registry identity the agent uses. The helper prints only a generic error on failure. Denial or an unreachable agent stops the command with no fallback. There's no offline mode: the agent must be reachable even for cached content.
The client's output and exit code pass through unchanged. With --json, they're captured in the usual oyzu exec result.

Code Cause Fix NATIVE_SESSION_CONFIG The endpoint is set in project or local configuration Move it to user or administrator configuration NATIVE_SESSION_UNAVAILABLE The agent can't be reached. The command hasn't started Start the agent and retry NATIVE_SESSION_DENIED The agent refused the request Get access granted; don't work around the agent NATIVE_SESSION_INVALID The endpoint isn't 127.0.0.1 HTTP, or the response is too large Fix the endpoint or the agent OCI_SESSION_INVALID The response or its registry addresses aren't valid Fix the agent's response OCI_ROUTING_CONFLICT Credential or source-policy overrides, duplicate mappings, a destination on an unlisted registry, or a changed digest Remove the override or fix the mapping OCI_OPERATION_UNSUPPORTED An unsupported command, publishing, or a cache reference without a grant Use a supported command and get the cache grant. Publish with oyzu publish OCI_SHIM_INVALID The generated shims are damaged Recreate them by activating the shell again

Not a general Docker CLI integration. Arbitrary Dockerfiles, dynamic arguments and transitive dependencies aren't checked by oyzu beyond the source policy. oyzu doesn't record which source each image came from in a report. Temporary files may be left behind if oyzu is killed. OCI credential-session shims are not available on Windows or macOS. Ordinary tool shims are a separate feature.
Helm installation Private Maven repositories

CLI reference Published from the canonical docs/reference/os-package-locks.md file. Features marked experimental remain experimental; check support limitations before relying on them. oyzu lock writes debs.lock.yaml and apks.lock.yaml for Docker targets. Each lock records every Debian or Alpine package file an image installs, with its URL, version, checksum and Package URL. Commit the lock with your change. Once a target has a lock, oyzu build installs from it: RUN steps see only a local snapshot repository that serves the locked files (see Frozen builds). Note: OS package locks are experimental. See Limitations for what isn't supported yet. oyzu pin locks tool versions. oyzu lock does not. Platform scope: Use an x64 host and supported x64 build targets. ARM64 is unsupported. Feature-specific limits are listed in the support matrix. A newer min_oyzu_version is advisory when the lock is understood. A refresh that would discard unknown fields refuses with FILE_READER_TOO_OLD and exit 3, preserving the lock bytes. The loss check runs before Docker observation and again before writing, against the existing lock's understood fields. When all fields are understood, updates may remove packages or architectures, and a family no longer installed may have its lock deleted. Compatible rewrites retain the higher marker. See file compatibility. Optional descriptive fields may be read without changing the lock. Vendor, format, package/source identity and the frozen snapshot's digest checks remain mandatory. A malformed recorded Debian index list is an OS_PACKAGE_LOCK_INVALID error; native index discovery is used only when the observation is absent. Repair or regenerate the observation with oyzu lock before retrying; a read never silently replaces it.

You change nothing in build.yaml or your Dockerfile. For each docker/image target, oyzu lock: Finds the stages that contribute to the final image (through FROM <stage>, COPY --from and RUN --mount=from=) and have at least one RUN. Pins each external base to its index digest and pulls it for this host's platform. A tag keeps the digest already in the lock unless you pass --update. Builds each of those stages once with docker buildx build --load --target, using the pinned bases and the host's network. This runs your own RUN steps. Copies the package database out of each built stage and its base (/var/lib/dpkg/status or /lib/apk/db/installed) without starting either, and takes the difference. That difference is the lock. Oyzu never parses the RUN shell, so a literal apt-get install, a variable, a heredoc or a copied script all lock the same packages. Looks up where each new package comes from (see below). Writes the lock next to the Dockerfile and prints what changed. For step 5: Debian and Ubuntu. apt runs inside the built stage (apt-get update, apt-get download --print-uris, apt-cache madison) and checks each repository's signed InRelease against the image's own keyring. The URL, size and SHA-256 come from that verified metadata. Any apt signature warning fails with OS_PACKAGE_UNVERIFIED, because apt can report a bad signature as a warning and carry on. Alpine. Oyzu reads /etc/apk/repositories and /etc/apk/arch from the built stage, fetches each repository's APKINDEX.tar.gz, finds the exact version, downloads the .apk, checks its size against the index and records its SHA-256. Package files and repository metadata seen while locking are kept by SHA-256 in a local store (<user data>/os-packages/blobs), ready for frozen builds.

oyzu lock Write missing locks and regenerate stale ones oyzu lock --check Fail if any lock is missing or stale; writes nothing oyzu lock --update Re-observe every lock with fresh bases and no build cache oyzu lock --update api Re-observe only the api target's locks (or name a lock path) oyzu lock --inputs --json List locked packages and bases for Renovate; resolves nothing Every form accepts the global --json flag. $ oyzu lock api-image locked 9 OS packages (2 requested, 7 dependencies) in services/api/debs.lock.yaml note: commit services/api/debs.lock.yaml with your change "Requested" packages are those apt did not mark Auto-Installed, or that are new in Alpine's /etc/apk/world.

Docker with Linux containers and buildx on PATH (Docker Desktop on Windows, or Docker Engine on Linux) Network access to the base image registry and the distribution mirrors. The usual HTTPS_PROXY, NO_PROXY and SSL_CERT_FILE settings apply to Oyzu's own Alpine downloads. If the selected Docker plugin has not been adopted for the project, run a real oyzu build in the same project root first. It records the normal builder selection in oyzu.lock, including for a Docker-only project with no tool requests. oyzu pin locks tool versions and does not adopt a plugin, and oyzu lock leaves that selection unchanged. oyzu lock observes this host's architecture: amd64 or arm64 (x86_64 or aarch64 in Alpine terms). One lock can hold both. Run oyzu lock on an amd64 host and on an arm64 host: each run keeps the other architecture's entries while the stages, base digests and install steps they came from are unchanged, and --update leaves the other architecture's versions alone. When those inputs changed, the other architecture's entries are dropped and the output says which host must lock again. A stage that isn't the last needs a name (AS <name>), because BuildKit can only target named stages.

# debs.lock.yaml, written by oyzu lock. Do not edit; run `oyzu lock` after changing the Dockerfile. lockfileVersion: 1 lockfileVendor: oyzu inputDigest: sha256:9f2c… stages: - stage: '0' base: docker.io/library/python@sha256:a6e3… observed: true arches: - arch: amd64 repositories: - repoid: debian-bookworm uri: http://deb.debian.org/debian suite: bookworm release: sha256:61d0… packages: - url: http://deb.debian.org/debian/pool/main/p/postgresql-15/libpq5_15.8-0%2bdeb12u1_amd64.deb repoid: debian-bookworm name: libpq5 evr: 15.8-0+deb12u1 checksum: sha256:7a3c… size: 191234 purl: pkg:deb/debian/libpq5@15.8-0%2Bdeb12u1?arch=amd64&distro=debian-12 sourcerpm: postgresql-15 requested: true stage: '0' url, repoid, checksum and size follow Hermeto's lock schema. name, evr and sourcerpm follow rpm-lockfile-prototype. inputDigest, stages, repositories, purl, requested and stage are Oyzu's own. Unnamed stages are named by index. Packages are sorted by name, version and stage, and there are no timestamps, so the same inputs and repository state give the same bytes. release is the SHA-256 of the repository's verified InRelease (apt) or of the APKINDEX.tar.gz that held the package (apk). url is the live mirror URL that apt or apk used. A Dockerfile whose stages use both Debian and Alpine bases gets both files. When an image stops installing one kind of package, oyzu lock removes that file.

A lock is stale when its inputDigest no longer matches the current inputs. For each locked stage, the digest covers: the FROM references and the stage's instructions up to its last RUN that looks like a package install, including the same part of any stage it starts from the contents of build-context files that COPY or ADD instructions in that part read, with line endings normalized so Windows and Linux checkouts agree the stage's pinned base digest It also covers global ARG lines and the set of locked architectures. A RUN looks like an install when it names apt-get, apt, aptitude, dpkg or apk, or runs a file copied earlier in the stage. This only decides where the digest stops. A miss can make a lock look stale, or let a later frozen build fail with OS_PACKAGE_NOT_LOCKED. It never produces a wrong lock. Files copied after the last install, such as application source, never make the lock stale. oyzu lock --check works offline. A digest-pinned FROM is compared with the lock's base. A tag keeps the lock's digest for the same repository, so a tag that moves upstream makes the lock behind, not stale. oyzu lock --update picks up the new digest. The reasons a lock is stale, in the order Oyzu checks them: A locked stage was removed. Its base digest changed. Its FROM now names another repository. A stage now installs packages and is in no lock. This host's architecture isn't locked. The Dockerfile or the files its install steps copy changed.

{ "format": 1, "mode": "write", "outcome": "written", "locks": [ { "path": "services/api/debs.lock.yaml", "target": "api-image", "reason": "base digest changed for stage 0 (… -> …)", "written": true, "packages": 9, "requested": 2, "changes": [ {"purl": "pkg:deb/debian/libpq5?arch=amd64&distro=debian-12", "stage": "0", "from": "15.7-0+deb12u1", "to": "15.8-0+deb12u1", "requested": true} ] } ] } mode is write, update, check or inputs. outcome is written or current for writes, current or stale for --check, and listed for --inputs. A change with no from is an added package, and one with no to was removed. reason is created, update, removed, current or the stale reason. architectures lists the architectures the written lock holds, and droppedArchitectures, present only when not empty, those whose entries were dropped because their inputs changed. --check entries carry status (current, stale or missing). For the last two they also carry code: OS_PACKAGE_LOCK_STALE, reason and fix: oyzu lock. A missing entry's path is the target's folder. --inputs entries list dependencies. Each base is {depName, currentDigest, datasource: docker}. Each package is {depName, currentValue, datasource: deb|apk, registryUrl, purl, requested, stage}. A Debian registryUrl carries Renovate's suite, components and binaryArch parameters.

When a Docker target has debs.lock.yaml or apks.lock.yaml, oyzu build prepares a snapshot repository before it runs anything. It never writes the lock. A stale lock fails with OS_PACKAGE_LOCK_STALE. Run oyzu lock first. For the host architecture, Oyzu collects each locked Debian repository's InRelease and the index files it lists (also under by-hash), each Alpine APKINDEX.tar.gz, and every locked package file. They come from the local store at <user data>/os-packages/blobs. Missing packages are downloaded and must match the lock's checksum and size. apt may keep its lists recompressed, so for each index apt read when you locked (recorded under <user data>/os-packages/indexes, or else each component's Packages), Oyzu downloads a variant that the InRelease signs by hash when the store has none, and checks that hash. The prepared tree (index.json mapping URL to SHA-256, plus blobs/) is copied into the BuildKit worker, which has no network, and served by oyzu-docker-snapshot on 127.0.0.1:3128. The build plan records its content store and tree_digest under actions[].extensions."oyzu.dev/executor".os_packages. RUN steps get host networking inside the worker (--allow network.host, which only reaches loopback there) and http_proxy and https_proxy build arguments that point at the server. apt verifies the served InRelease with the image's own keyring and every file against its checksums, as it did when you locked. The server always answers with the full locked file and never 304 Not Modified, so lists an image already carries (python:*-slim ships an InRelease) can't stand in for the locked metadata. A request for anything not in the lock gets a 404. The failed build reports OS_PACKAGE_NOT_LOCKED naming the package, in its error output and its retained log. Targets without a lock build as before. The snapshot server, oyzu-docker-snapshot, ships in the Docker plugin package and is mounted into the BuildKit worker, so the worker image needs nothing extra. A Docker plugin package built without its Linux helpers can't serve the snapshot.

Exit Meaning 0 Locks written or already current; --check found every lock current 1 An error, such as a failed observation build 2 Invalid command arguments 3 Configuration or policy validation failed 4 --check found a missing or stale lock

Code When Recovery PLUGIN_NOT_ADOPTED The selected Docker builder has no adopted selection in the project's oyzu.lock Run oyzu build in the same project root to adopt the builder selection, then run oyzu lock OS_PACKAGE_LOCK_STALE --check found a missing or stale lock oyzu lock OS_PACKAGE_UNRESOLVABLE apt or apk can't find an installed version in the stage's repositories, for example a .deb installed by file, or a version replaced upstream between the build and the lookup Install from a configured repository, or run oyzu lock again OS_PACKAGE_UNVERIFIED apt reported a signature problem, or a repository has no signed InRelease Fix the repository's signing key in the image OS_PACKAGE_UNAVAILABLE Oyzu couldn't download an Alpine index or package, a locked file no longer matches its checksum, or a frozen build needs signed metadata that this machine's store lacks (a lock written elsewhere) Check network and proxy settings, or run oyzu lock --update on this machine OS_PACKAGE_NOT_LOCKED A frozen build's RUN step asked for a package file that the lock doesn't contain oyzu lock --update, or remove the install OS_PACKAGE_METADATA_EXPIRED A frozen build's locked Debian InRelease is past its Valid-Until oyzu lock --update OS_PACKAGE_UPDATE_SELECTOR --update pkg:… selects a single package Update the whole lock or its target A failed observation build shows the last lines of BuildKit's output.

Run oyzu lock --check in CI or before you merge. It works offline, writes nothing and exits with status 4 when a lock is missing or stale. A frozen oyzu build then confirms that the image installs only locked packages: anything else fails with OS_PACKAGE_NOT_LOCKED.

Frozen builds replay the original metadata. Debian metadata past its Valid-Until, or missing from this machine's store, can't be rebuilt, so those builds fail with OS_PACKAGE_METADATA_EXPIRED or OS_PACKAGE_UNAVAILABLE. Alpine over HTTPS. The snapshot server terminates TLS for locked Alpine hosts, but its certificate authority can't yet be added to RUN steps, so HTTPS Alpine repositories fail certificate checks in frozen builds. One architecture per host. oyzu lock observes, and frozen builds serve, only the host's architecture. A lock gets another architecture's entries only from a run on a host of that architecture. They're kept only while both architectures install in the same stages, so a Dockerfile that installs packages in a stage on one architecture only can lock one architecture at a time. Locking uses the host network. The observation build has the host's ordinary network. Oyzu checks the lock against the package manager's own metadata, not against a record of the files fetched. No single-package updates. --update pkg:deb/debian/libpq5 is refused. Not available: input files (debs.in.yaml), --suggest, RPM locks, snapshot-service URLs, and Alpine index signature checks. Oyzu relies on HTTPS for APKINDEX.tar.gz, and the size check ties each .apk to the fetched index. Dockerfile reading covers stages, global ARG defaults, line continuations, heredocs and COPY --from and RUN --mount=from=. .dockerignore isn't applied to the digest, and files read by RUN --mount=type=bind aren't covered. A RUN that runs a script it bind-mounts from the build context still counts as an install, so its stage is observed and locked. A later edit to that script leaves the lock current, and a frozen build refuses any package it adds. Related: Docker images, Docker quality checks.
CLI reference Published from the canonical docs/reference/oyzu-toml.md file. Features marked experimental remain experimental; check support limitations before relying on them.

[tests] controls in-build retries. tests.retries is an integer from zero through 65535, defaulting to zero locally and two in pr, ci, and release. tests.flaky is "pass" (default) or "fail". Both support context overrides and policy locks; retry counts support policy maximums. See test retries for guards, cache behavior and examples. oyzu.toml says how, where and how strictly your builds run: tool versions, environment variables, tasks, check levels, caching and the values that change between your laptop, a pull request and a release. It never says what is built; native manifests and build.yaml do that. Most projects need no oyzu.toml at all. Add one when you want to pin a tool, add a task, or change a default. The complete list shows every setting the CLI accepts. Platform scope: Use an x64 host and supported x64 build targets. ARM64 is unsupported. Feature-specific limits are listed in the support matrix. The top-level min_oyzu_version string records the minimum reader the owner declares for the content, written only when the content requires a reader newer than the marker baseline (0.3.5) (for example "0.3.6"). It is file metadata and cannot be overridden by profiles, contexts or toolsets. See minimum reader version for the advisory upgrade notice, required-feature refusals and update guidance. A newer marker alone warns once and allows understood settings. Unsupported [compatibility].requires entries still stop execution; a newer declaration supplies an attributed upgrade target when the first supporting release is unknown.

#:schema https://github.com/oyzuai/oyzu-releases/releases/latest/download/oyzu.toml.schema.json # Tool versions. A prefix ("22") picks the newest matching release; # oyzu.lock records the exact version for every platform. [tools] node = "22" go = "1.27.3" # Environment for tasks, builds and activated shells. [env] APP_MODE = "development" # A task: run it with `oyzu run seed`. [tasks.seed] argv = ["node", "scripts/seed.mjs"] # How strict each check is. Fast local builds run only `required` checks. [checks] lint = "advisory" coverageMinimum = 70 # Stricter values for one context: local, pr, ci or release. [context.release.checks] tests = "required" coverageMinimum = 85 # Build-wide scheduling and caching. [build] jobs = 8 [cache] local = true # A named set of other tool versions, for verification runs in CI. [toolsets.node24] tools.node = "24" Check it without running anything: oyzu config validate --strict oyzu config explain checks.coverageMinimum

Oyzu reads several files and combines them. A nearer, more specific file wins over a farther one. File Where Typical use Commit it? Machine configuration Windows: ProgramData Oyzu\config.toml; macOS: /Library/Application Support/Oyzu/config.toml; Linux: /etc/oyzu/config.toml Defaults for everyone on a host — User configuration Windows: RoamingAppData Oyzu\config.toml; macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/Oyzu/config.toml; Linux: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/oyzu/config.toml (else ~/.config/oyzu/config.toml) Your personal defaults, credentials destinations, trust — Root oyzu.toml The project root (the Git top level) Team settings for the whole project Yes Folder oyzu.toml Any folder below the root Settings for the builds in that folder Yes oyzu.local.toml Next to any oyzu.toml Personal overrides for one checkout No Invocation Flags such as --jobs, --profile; OYZU_* variables One command — OYZU_USER_CONFIG=/absolute/path.toml replaces the user file, which is useful for disposable environments. The order, lowest first: built-in defaults, organization policy defaults, machine, user, each oyzu.toml from the root down to the build's folder, each oyzu.local.toml in the same order, then the invocation. Each file applies its base values, then its context values, then the selected profile. Administrative policy and [constraints] are applied last and cannot be overridden by an ordinary file. Values replace, they don't merge. A list in a nearer file replaces the whole list; a task in a nearer file replaces the whole task record. To delete an inherited environment variable or task, see [overrides]. In CI, user configuration (other than presentation settings) and oyzu.local.toml files are left out, so a CI build depends only on committed files. --local-overrides asks for local files, if policy allows it. To see where a value came from: oyzu config explain build.jobs oyzu config show --json

Section Holds Can be set in [tools] Tool versions Any file [env] Environment variables, PATH additions Any file [tasks.<name>] Commands for oyzu run and build hooks Any file [checks] Test, coverage, lint and format levels Any file [build] Parallelism, isolation, optimization, executors Any file [cache] Local and remote action cache Any file (remote destinations: user or machine) [context.<name>] Values for local, pr, ci or release Any file [profiles.<name>] Named sets of values chosen with --profile Any file [toolsets.<name>] Alternative tool versions for verification runs Project files [constraints] Rules no folder can undercut Root oyzu.toml only [overrides] Removal of inherited entries Any file [compatibility] Required CLI capabilities Any file [verification] Tool lines a release must be verified on Any file [scan] and [analysis] Secret scanning, static-analysis rules Any file [publish] oyzu publish destinations and evidence Root oyzu.toml and oyzu.local.toml, user, machine Builder sections [docker], [maven], [npm] Any file [ui], [version], [profile] Color, version inference, default profile Any file [settings] Developer-command auto-install behavior Any file User and machine settings Tool index and catalog, platform, trust, plugins, engines User or machine only Administrative settings Allowed tools, profiles, routes, sources Policy only A section name Oyzu doesn't know produces a warning (with a spelling hint when it is close to a known one) and has no effect; oyzu config validate --strict turns those warnings into errors. A build.yaml key written here, such as [builds.web], only gets this warning from the CLI; the editor schema points out that it belongs in build.yaml.

Tool versions, by tool name. Oyzu resolves each request to an exact version, records it in oyzu.lock, installs it once into the shared tool store and puts it on PATH for builds, tasks and shells. [tools] node = "22" # newest 22.x go = "1.27.3" # exactly 1.27.3 rust = "1.99.1" "oyzu:gh" = { version = "2.49.2" } # table form; same meaning Key Values Default Meaning tools.<name> A version request string ("22", "1.27", "1.27.3", "latest"), or { version = "…" } none Requests that tool. A prefix selects the newest matching release; latest the newest eligible one. Short names (node) and canonical ids ("oyzu:node") name the same tool. tools.ignore List of tool names none Silences best-effort tool detection for builds in this folder and below. Never removes a primary toolchain; an explicit [tools] entry still provides the tool. tools.lockPlatforms Nonempty list of exact platforms, such as linux/amd64/gnu Every build's declared platforms plus this host The platforms oyzu.lock records tool versions for (the host is always included). Can't vary by profile or context, and doesn't change which platforms are built. See lock platform coverage. tools.minimumReleaseAgeDays Integer 7–65535 7 Minimum publication age for moving default tool selections. Organization policy can impose a longer minimum; an exact younger pin warns. Only signed-index security metadata can grant an exception. See publisher evidence. Native pins come first. A version a native file already pins (rust-toolchain.toml, Go's go.mod minimum, and others as each ecosystem is adopted) is the request; a [tools] value in the same or a nearer folder must agree with it. See tools and toolchains. Tools never vary by profile or context. [profiles.x.tools] and [context.release.tools] are refused; use a toolset to try other versions. Edit with commands instead of by hand: oyzu install node@22, oyzu update, oyzu uninstall node. See tool commands.

Environment variables for tasks, builds and activated shells. [env] APP_MODE = "development" [env._] path = { prepend = ["tools/bin"] } # relative to this file Key Values Default Meaning env.<NAME> A string, or { secret = "<reference>" } none Sets the variable. Names use ASCII letters, digits and _, starting with a letter or _; the OYZU_ prefix is reserved. Values are literal: no interpolation. Secret references are accepted but not yet delivered to tasks. env._.path A list of folders, or { prepend = […], append = […] } none Adds folders to PATH, relative to the declaring file. A nearer file's value replaces a farther one's. Literal values can enter build inputs and evidence, so never put a secret in [env]. Inspection redacts credential-like names, but that does not make [env] a secret store. See shell activation for how [env] reaches your shell and how it is restored when you leave the folder.

Commands you run with oyzu run <name>, and hooks that run around build stages (pre_build, post_test and so on). In a multi-target project, prefix the target: [tasks."api:test"]. [tasks.seed] argv = ["node", "scripts/seed.mjs"] # argument array: no shell env = { SEED_SIZE = "small" } [tasks.lint] run = "eslint . && prettier --check ." # a shell command shell = "bash" [tasks."api:post_build"] argv = ["node", "scripts/stamp.mjs"] outputs = ["dist/stamp.json"] cache = true # hooks still run every build Field Values Meaning run String A shell command. Use either run or argv. Extra arguments after -- are refused. argv List of strings A program and its arguments, with no shell. Arguments after oyzu run name -- are appended. Elements may use {namespace.name} placeholders. shell String The shell for run, such as bash or sh. cwd Path Working directory, relative to the declaring oyzu.toml. env Table of strings Variables for this task only. depends_on List of task names Tasks to run first. inputs List of paths Extra inputs for caching (inside the target). outputs List of paths Files the task produces. cache Boolean With outputs, requests reuse by oyzu build; complete read admission is also required. Hooks always run. See authored tasks. interactive Boolean Keep the real terminal instead of capturing output to dist/logs. reports Report declarations Test and coverage reports the task writes: kind, format, path, and optional owner. A named redirect resolves the exact frozen native report-owner key; other owners retain their defaults. See npm aggregate test reports. when, unless Condition table Plan-time conditions (context, platform…). See task and hook conditions. A nearer file's task replaces the whole record; fields are never merged. See build tasks for hooks, streams and limits.

How strict each check is, and which checks a build runs. [checks] format = "off" lint = "advisory" coverageMinimum = 70 Key Values Default Meaning checks.tests off · advisory · enforce · required enforce Level for the test stage. checks.coverage same enforce Level for coverage collection. checks.lint same enforce Level for linters. checks.format same enforce Level for format checks. checks.run required · all required; all in pr, ci and release Which checks a build runs: only required ones, or every check that is not off. checks.coverageMinimum Integer 0–100 0 Minimum line coverage, in percent. A positive minimum requires coverage evidence. checks.quarantineFlaky true · false false Waive only admitted same-key flaky assertion failures, keeping each failure visible. Protected policy can forbid it. See flaky-test quarantine. Level Runs in When it fails off never; its tools are not even prepared — advisory builds that run every check a warning; the build succeeds enforce builds that run every check the build fails required every build, including a fast local one the build fails So a plain local oyzu build runs only required checks, CI runs everything that is not off, and oyzu build --full runs everything locally. See check levels.

Key Values Default Meaning build.jobs Integer 1–65535 the machine's logical CPUs How many independent actions run at once. --jobs N / -j N and OYZU_BUILD_JOBS override it. Doesn't affect cache keys. build.failFast true · false true Per target: a build-failing failure stops the whole build when true; false blocks only dependents. Nearest folder wins; context beats base in the same file. --keep-going / --fail-fast, then OYZU_BUILD_FAIL_FAST, override files subject to constraints. Doesn't affect cache keys. See failure behavior. build.installExecutables Boolean true Copy successfully collected executables to .oyzu/bin. Set false to keep them in the bundle only; normal per-target cascade and policy constraints apply. Oyzu’s checkout sets false. build.bundleDirectory dist · .oyzu/bundle dist Where Oyzu writes its bundle. Set it in the root files or user or machine configuration; component files are refused. One destination applies to the whole build. See bundle destination. build.isolation auto · docker · crun auto Which sandbox runs isolated Node steps on Linux: Docker when available, otherwise the daemonless crun sandbox. build.optimized true · false unset Unset: optimize only when output leaves the machine (release, remote cache, image packaging). Set: always optimized or always development. --optimized / --no-optimized override it. build.executors.<platform> host · cross-toolchain · container unset The only executor allowed to build that platform (linux/arm64, aliases accepted). If it's unavailable the platform is skipped with a reason. build.host-workspaces-dir Absolute path per-user native cache folder, or the Git directory when that is on another drive Where native host builds park their private source projections between builds. User or machine only, outside the source tree; never part of an action key. See source parking. [build] jobs = 4 [build.executors] "linux/arm64" = "container" [context.release.build] optimized = true See optimized builds and platforms and executors.

Key Values Default Meaning cache.trustNativeTestReads true · false false Opt in to trusted native Rust test reuse using full Cargo package inputs. Policy can lock it off; no profiles. cache.local true · false true Reuse results of unchanged actions from the local action cache. --no-cache bypasses it once. cache.nativeMaxMiB Integer MiB, 1–1048576 8192 (8 GiB) Total size kept for native compiler caches (Rust). cache.dockerMaxMiB Integer MiB, 1–1048576 20480 (20 GiB) Total size of Docker images Oyzu pulled; least recently used go first. cache.read true · false true Consult the remote cache after a local miss. cache.write true · false false Push local results to the remote cache. cache.immutableTags true · false false Declare that the remote registries refuse to replace a tag. Ignored for REAPI. cache.remote oci://host[:port]/repository/prefix, grpc://loopback[:port]/instance or grpcs://host[:port]/instance unset The shared remote action cache. User or machine only. cache.ciRemote same unset The CI-only cache: CI reads and writes it; other builds only read it. User or machine only. cache.remoteHeader Lowercase application metadata header unset REAPI only: send OYZU_CACHE_TOKEN verbatim under this header instead of the default bearer metadata. User or machine only, no profiles. cache.remoteClientCert Absolute PEM certificate file path unset REAPI mTLS client certificate; set with cache.remoteClientKey. User or machine only. cache.remoteClientKey Absolute PEM private-key file path unset REAPI mTLS client key; set with cache.remoteClientCert. User or machine only. cache.dir Absolute path per-user cache folder Where the local action cache lives. User or machine only. Remote cache credentials are never settings: they come from OYZU_CACHE_TOKEN or the CI job's ID-token flow. The mTLS settings contain only paths; private-key bytes and token values never belong in TOML. OYZU_CACHE_REMOTE and OYZU_CACHE_CI_REMOTE set the destinations for one invocation. See action cache.

Values that apply only in one build context. <name> is exactly local, pr, ci or release; the context is detected from the CI provider and Git ref, or forced with --context or OYZU_CONTEXT. [checks] coverageMinimum = 50 [context.pr.checks] coverageMinimum = 70 [context.release] checks.coverageMinimum = 90 build.optimized = true Write settings under it as you would at the top level. Settings that a profile can't hold can't vary by context either (trust controls, directories, profile.default, plugin and engine bindings, session endpoints); the Scope column marks them "no profiles or contexts". Within one file, a context value beats the base value and an inferred ci profile, but loses to a profile you chose with --profile. Between files, the nearer file still wins: a folder's base value beats the root's [context.release] value. To vary a folder by context, put a context table in that folder's file. Tools can't vary by context, and build-wide settings (build.jobs, cache.*, ui.color…) take context values only in the root file. See per-context values and build context.

A named set of values you choose per command with --profile <name> (or OYZU_PROFILE). [profile] default picks one when nothing else does. [profile] default = "dev" [profiles.dev.build] jobs = 3 [profiles.integration.env] API_URL = "http://localhost:8080" oyzu --profile integration run test oyzu --no-profile build oyzu config profiles A profile never grants authority and never changes tools (CONFIG_PROFILE_TOOLS; use a toolset). Settings that pick executable code or trust (plugins.*, engines.*, trust.*, directories and keys) are refused in profiles. In CI with no profile chosen, Oyzu's built-in ci profile applies, which sets checks.run = "all".

Other tool versions to verify a build with, without changing what ships. Each toolset adds a verification run (build and test stages, no artifact) for builds whose builder uses one of its tools. [tools] node = "22" [toolsets.node24] tools.node = "24" contexts = ["ci", "release"] # default: every context except local platforms = ["linux/x86_64"] # default: one run on the build's first platform Field Values Default Meaning tools Table like [tools] — The versions this toolset replaces. Tools it doesn't name keep their [tools] value. contexts List of local · pr · ci · release pr, ci, release Contexts whose builds add this toolset's verification run. [] turns it off. platforms List of os/arch[/abi] the build's first platform One verification run per listed platform. oyzu --toolset node24 exec -- node --version oyzu build --verify-with node24 Toolsets live in project files (oyzu.toml, oyzu.local.toml) only, not in profiles, contexts, user or machine configuration. The nearest definition of a name applies whole. See toolsets and verification toolsets.

Rules that hold in every folder of the project. Only the root oyzu.toml may contain [constraints]; they apply after every ordinary value, so no folder can undercut them. Name the setting by its full key, in quotes. # root oyzu.toml [constraints."checks.tests"] minimum = "required" when = { context = ["release"] } [constraints."checks.coverageMinimum"] minimum = 60 [[constraints."build.optimized"]] locked = true value = true when = { context = ["release"] } Field Meaning locked + value The setting is exactly this value. allowed The value must be one of these. minimum, maximum Bounds for numbers and ordered levels (off < advisory < enforce < required). required Items a list must contain. when, unless Selectors: context, provider, path (relative to the root). Settings that only user or machine files can hold, administrative settings, env.* and tasks.* can't be constrained here. See project constraints.

Removes entries inherited from farther files. [overrides] remove = ["env.DEMO_MODE", "tasks.hello"] Key Values Meaning overrides.remove List of env.<NAME> and tasks.<name> keys Removes those inherited entries. A removed variable is also unset in development tasks.

Declares what a CLI must understand to read this file correctly. An older CLI that lacks a required capability fails instead of silently ignoring a setting. [compatibility] schema_major = 1 requires = ["config.env-path/v1"] Key Values Meaning compatibility.schema_major 1 The configuration format's major version. compatibility.requires List of capabilities Capabilities the reader must support: config.cascade/v1, config.profiles/v1, config.removal/v1, config.env-path/v1, policy.constraints/v1.

Key Values Default Meaning verification.<tool> List of tool lines ("22", "3.12", "1.24.5") none The versions of that tool (named without a namespace: node, not oyzu:node) a build needs passing verification evidence for before oyzu publish accepts it. A line no toolset covers adds a verification run. [verification] node = ["22", "24"] See required tool lines.

Key Values Default Meaning scan.jobs Integer 1–65535 2 How many independent scan checks run at once. scan.gitleaks.enabled true · false false Select Gitleaks secret scanning for oyzu scan (experimental). scan.gitleaks.failOnFindings true · false false Fail on any Gitleaks finding. It can only tighten an administrative selection. analysis.rules Table of rule id → off · advisory · enforce every rule advisory Static-analysis rule levels (experimental). Unknown ids are errors that list valid ids. analysis.suppress List of { rule, path?, reason } none Suppress findings; reason is required. Unmatched suppressions are reported as stale. [scan.gitleaks] enabled = true failOnFindings = true [analysis.rules] phantom-dependency = "enforce" [[analysis.suppress]] rule = "escaping-reference" path = "legacy/**" reason = "vendored fork" See scan and node static analysis.

Destinations and evidence for oyzu publish. Among project files only the root oyzu.toml and oyzu.local.toml may set these; a [publish] table in a component folder is an error. User and machine configuration may set them too. Each value is replaced whole by a nearer source, never merged. Key Values Meaning publish.default Destination or set name Used when oyzu publish has no --destination. publish.destinations Table of name → { registry, repository, usernameEnv?, passwordEnv? } OCI registries to publish to. Auto-install behavior of the developer commands (oyzu exec, shims, missing commands, oyzu run). Builds always require their complete locked tool selection, whatever these say. These decide trust, credential destinations or executable code.
